publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: Multi source energy supply systems are affected by various uncertain factors in actual operation, such as the volatility of renewable energy, uncertainty of load demand, equipment failures, etc. In order to cope with these uncertain factors and address the problems of poor reliability and low response speed, this paper proposes a multi-source energy supply collaborative control algorithm under load response optimization. Calculate the load of multi-source energy supply, and construct a multi-source energy supply collaborative control model with the annual investment and operation cost, CO2 pollutant emissions, and multi-source energy supply interruption rate as objective functions. On this basis, a multi-objective hybrid particle swarm algorithm is adopted to establish an external Pareto solution set archive, record all non dominated collaborative control schemes, solve the multi-source energy supply collaborative control model, and achieve multi-source energy supply collaborative control. The experimental results show that the proposed method has a good collaborative control effect on multi-source energy supply, which can effectively improve the economy, environmental protection, and reliability of multi-source energy supply, and has a high response speed.

Author Keywords: Multi objective hybrid particle swarm algorithm

articleTitle: Research on Dynamic Assessment for Conductor Sag of Overhead Transmission Lines under Extreme Operating Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: The sag of overhead transmission lines are crucial indicators for the safe operation of the lines. In China, the maximum allowable temperature for long-term operation of conductors differs from the temperature used for sag calculation during tower installation. Under extreme operating conditions, the issues of sag distance in heavily loaded lines cannot be ignored. Therefore, this paper proposes a method for dynamically assessing the sag of overhead transmission lines under extreme operating conditions. The proposed method is validated using overload experimental data from a real 35kV overhead line in a certain region. The validation results indicate that the error between the calculated sag and the measured sag is less than 6%, basically meeting engineering requirements. Finally, based on the model proposed in this paper, a method for sag over-limit warning of overhead transmission lines under extreme operating conditions is proposed.

articleTitle: Research on Critical Oxygen Concentration in Oxy-MILD Combustion of Syngas Fuel Using Artificial Neural Networks Method
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: This study investigates the critical oxygen concentration for oxy-fuel moderate or intense low oxygen dilution (Oxy-MILD) combustion of syngas. Syngas, composed of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, CO, and CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, presents unique challenges for achieving stable MILD combustion due to its distinct chemical activity. This research employs two predictive models, multiple linear regression (MLR) and artificial neural networks (ANN), to analyze the relationship between oxygen concentration and the molar fractions of syngas components. The results show that while the MLR provides reasonable accuracy for data with small deviations, the ANN model outperforms it in terms of prediction accuracy, particularly for more complex, non-linear scenarios. This study highlights the potential of ANN models in predicting critical combustion parameters and offers valuable insights for optimizing combustion processes in industrial settings, demonstrating the applicability of advanced machine learning techniques in combustion research.

articleTitle: Research on the Capacity Configuration Method of Micro-Pumped Storage Based on the Common Reservoir Operation Mode in Low-Pressure Area
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: To improve the energy interaction level between substations while reducing the construction cost of the micro-pumped storage system. This paper proposes a power and capacity configuration method for low-voltage substation pumped storage power systems under the common reservoir operation mode. The proposed method is based on the common reservoir operation mode, and opens up a waterway between substations to achieve energy transfer by connecting multiple reservoirs. Taking the control effect as a constraint, the power and capacity of the pumped storage system are reconfigured to achieve the purpose of maintaining the system control effect while saving construction costs. Simulation examples show that compared with the separate reservoir operation mode of the micro-pumped storage system, under the same performance, the common reservoir mode significantly reduces the reservoir capacity requirements by 39.23% through the common reservoir.

articleTitle: Research on Hybrid Energy Storage Configuration Method with Independent Operating Entities Participating in Frequency Regulation Auxiliary. services
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: ABSTRA CT-This article focuses on the research of energy storage configuration methods for hybrid energy storage power stations that participate in frequency regulation auxiliary services as independent operating entities. Firstly, a full life cycle cost model for a hybrid energy storage system consisting of lithium batteries and flow batteries was established, as well as a revenue model for participating in frequency regulation services as an independent energy storage power station; A method was proposed to achieve AGC(Automatic Generation Control) signal decomposition and allocation by optimizing the parameters of second-order Butterworth low-pass filters; On this basis, a hybrid energy storage capacity and power optimization configuration model was established, taking into account constraints such as battery charging and discharging depth, with the goal of maximizing frequency modulation benefits. Genetic algorithm was used to achieve nonlinear solution of the objective function; Finally, taking the actual AGC frequency modulation command as an example, the optimized configuration of hybrid energy storage was achieved.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Transmitter Coil Magnetically Coupled Resonance Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: The non-contact power supply approach can avoid many drawbacks of traditional wire-based power supply methods, ensuring the stability of wireless power transfer systems. This paper focuses on the working principle and system structure of magnetically coupled resonance wireless power transfer systems. Based on this, a system with multiple transmitter coils is designed, allowing the system's output power to remain constant under disturbances caused by variations in the coupling coefficient. The mutual inductance model and SS-type compensation structure are selected for design from a circuit perspective. A simulation model for the control design of the wireless power transfer system is built based on simulation software, and the whale optimization algorithm is utilized to tune and optimize the PID control parameters. Analysis of the optimized simulation results indicates that, with PID control, the system can achieve constant output power under variations in mutual inductance, i.e., changes in the coupling coefficient, and exhibits stronger disturbance rejection capabilities.

articleTitle: Source-Grid-Load-Storage Participates in the Research on Peak Regulation Strategies in the Power Market
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: Against the backdrop of the large-scale integration of new energy sources and the connection of a large number of users, the traditional power system architecture is facing new challenges. Based on the complex system theory, this research adopts the multi-agent technology to design a peak shaving control strategy with the coordinated participation of power generation sources, power grids, power loads, and energy storage systems. Through the peak shaving control mechanism, a win-win situation is achieved between the grid's peak shaving control requirements and the interests of various market entities. This paper not only provides the theoretical basis for peak shaving control but also verifies the effectiveness of the proposed strategy through simulation.

Author Keywords: Power Loads and Energy Storage Systems

articleTitle: Spatial-temporal Distribution Prediction of Electric Vehicle Charging Load Based on Charging Models
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for spatial-temporal distribution prediction of electric vehicles (EVs) charging loads based on a charging decision model. Firstly, using the origin-destination (OD) probability matrix to identify the starting and ending points for the travel of private cars, taxis, and other urban functional vehicles, while the Dijkstra algorithm is applied to optimize driving paths. Subsequently, combining the node impedance and the road segment impedance to establish a dynamic road network model, and calculate the weights of each road. Simultaneously, constructing the energy consumption model to calculate the power consumption during their operation. Then, according to the remaining battery, users are classified into random and demand types, and a charging decision-making model of EV users is proposed. Then, based on the multi-source information mentioned above, the EV charging load forecasting framework is established. Finally, Monte Carlo method is used to simulate the travel processes and charging behaviors of EVs, resulting in the spatial-temporal Distribution of charging loads. Designed a typical and regional road network EV charging load forecasting case, verifying the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Direct Torque Control of Dual Three-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Deadbeat
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: By combining the advantages of the deadbeat control strategy and direct torque control (DTC), a new control strategy for dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motors (DTP-PMSM) is proposed. Based on the mathematical model of the DTP-PMSM, the stator flux and rotor flux are used as state variables, and the motor's angular velocity is sampled to construct an extended state observer (ESO) in the stator magnetic field coordinate system. Simulation experiments were conducted based on the theoretical framework. The simulation results show that the system's torque and flux dynamic response are faster under the no-dead-time switching direct torque control strategy. Compared to traditional DTC methods for DTP-PMSM, the proposed approach significantly reduces flux and torque ripples, improves system robustness, and demonstrates excellent control performance.

articleTitle: Modeling of Smart Energy Cities Based on Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: Aiming at the smart energy city currently has a wide range of energy data sources, including electricity, natural gas, heat and many other different fields of energy data often have differences in format, standards and collection methods, making it difficult to achieve uniform integration and analysis problems. Based on deep neural network technology, this paper proposes a smart energy city model, aiming to construct a city physical examination index system under the energy perspective. Firstly, by integrating energy data from different fields such as electricity, gas and heat, and combining the three key elements of “people, land and housing”, a comprehensive and systematic city checkup evaluation model is constructed based on deep neural network. Secondly, on the basis of the existing city checkup evaluation system, the metadata, dimensions and calculation methods of each index are clarified to analyze the close relationship between energy use and urban development. The study shows that constructing a city checkup indicator system from the energy perspective can not only comprehensively reflect the city's energy utilization situation, but also promote the optimization of energy structure, reduce energy consumption, provide decision-making support for green and low-carbon development, and enhance the level of city management.

articleTitle: Design and Experiment of New Faraday Shielding Channel for CFETR ICRF Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: A new design concept for the flow channels within the Faraday shield of the ICRF antenna, directly facing the plasma, is proposed. Numerical simulations are conducted to compare two types of flow channels-traditional straight pipes and newly designed flow channels-under the same heating source conditions. During the numerical simulation, the same boundary conditions, heat flux density, flow rate of water in the pipe, and structural material (316L stainless steel) are applied. By comparing the maximum temperature of the flow channels under identical conditions, this work provides guidance for the design and optimization of flow channels in the Faraday shield of ICRF antennas in CFETR.

articleTitle: Particle Swarm Optimized Matched Tracking Algorithm for Power Line Channel Parameter Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: To improve the identification accuracy of multipath model parameters of low-voltage power line channel and reduce the identification time, a hybrid PSO-MP algorithm is proposed by integrating particle swarm optimization algorithm and matching tracking algorithm, and the problem of identifying parameters of low-voltage power line channel model is investigated by using this method. The results show that the PSO-MP hybrid algorithm integrates the complementary advantages of the two, and the channel parameter recognition accuracy based on the hybrid algorithm is higher than that of the genetic algorithm, PSO algorithm, and genetic matching tracking algorithm, respectively, and the accuracy will be improved with the increase of the number of paths; at the same time, the PSO-MP hybrid algorithm not only improves the channel model parameter recognition accuracy but also improves the convergence speed of the system. It can be seen that the low-voltage power line multipath model parameter identification method based on the PSO-MP hybrid algorithm is feasible and efficient.

articleTitle: Research on Machine Learning-Based Carbon Profiling Algorithm for Enterprises and Production Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: Carbon profiling technology provides scientific support for carbon emission management at both the enterprise and production line levels. At the enterprise level, it helps identify emission sources, optimize energy use, and assess the effectiveness of green energy, contributing to carbon reduction and brand image enhancement. At the production line level, it focuses on energy and carbon flow analysis, optimizing process flows, and reducing emission intensity. Through data collection, feature extraction, and model building, combined with machine learning algorithms, carbon profiling enables accurate quantification and dynamic adjustment of carbon emissions, supporting enterprises in predicting emission reduction potential and formulating energy-saving strategies. As a crucial tool for achieving carbon neutrality, carbon profiling enhances enterprise energy efficiency, drives green transformation, and provides data support for policy compliance and carbon trading. Its broad application prospects will continue to aid sustainable development.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Intelligent Sensors in Temperature Monitoring and Prediction in New Energy Storage Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: With the increasing global energy demand and the prominence of environmental issues, energy storage technology has gained significant attention in power system applications. This paper explores the application of intelligent sensors for temperature monitoring and prediction in new energy storage systems. Through a comprehensive literature review, intelligent sensors were summarized and categorized, with a focus on thermocouple-based temperature sensors. Calibration experiments on J-type, E-type, and K-type spring-loaded thermocouples were conducted, yielding Seebeck coefficients of 0.0535 mVI 0 C, 0.08129 mVI 0 C, and 0.0399 mVI 0 C, respectively, which verified their temperature measurement performance and reliability. The experimental results demonstrate that selecting appropriate intelligent sensors enables precise temperature monitoring and prediction in energy storage systems, thereby improving system operational efficiency and stability.

articleTitle: Research on Energy Consumption Optimization Effect of Calibration Strategy Based on CLTC
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: Energy consumption optimization has become research hot spot. To explore the impact of vehicle calibration strategies based on driving characteristics of CLTC on the energy consumption optimization of domestically operated vehicles, this paper takes a compact SUV that is calibrated for emissions and fuel consumption optimization based on WLTC as the research object and proposes a calibration strategy based on CLTC. Using the VSP-Bin partitioning method, a more microscopic perspective is used to study the optimization effect of vehicle energy consumption before and after calibration. The research results show that compared to WLTC, the proposed CLTC-based calibration strategy is more suitable for the real road traffic operation of vehicles in China, and the overall energy consumption is reduced by approximately 3.61 % after calibration.

articleTitle: Energy Storage Application and Development Prediction for Zhejiang Province
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: The proliferation of new energy storage systems is accelerating in China largely attributable to the incentivizing policies enacted by National Energy Administration. However, most of them are not in frequent use or in a proper way. In this paper, a new scenario is proposed that with the energy storage plant the PV plant can track the load power trend. The power capacity and stored energy are also calculated. A new scenario for wind power is proposed that its power curve is smoothed by energy storage. After that the power curves including the energy storage power are predicted for Zhejiang province. That gives the suggestion for the future energy storage installation in Zhejiang.

articleTitle: Research on Impedance Modeling and Grid Stability of Flexible Excitation Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: Synchronous machines based on conventional excitation are widely used in power systems, but their damping control effect is poor. The flexible excitation system proposed in recent years provides damping support to the system by adding damping channels based on the existing self-excited excitation system, thereby suppressing the risk of system oscillation. To analyze the grid stability of flexible excitation synchronous machines clearly and accurately, it is necessary to model the flexible excitation system. Using the impedance modeling method, an analytical model of the flexible excitation synchronous machine considering multiple control loops is derived and verified. Based on the derived model, the stability laws of grid connection are further analyzed and verified in conjunction with the electromagnetic transient simulation model.

articleTitle: Research on the Missing Cap Fault Detection Technology of Transmission Line Insulator Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: In order to obtain more accurate and general detection performance, based on the feature pyramid structure and local attention mechanism, this paper proposes an improved algorithm LAPF based on Faster R-CNN to improve the detection accuracy of insulators and defects. Firstly, aiming at the problems of low detection accuracy caused by blurred insulator edges, small defect targets, and easy loss of details during detection, the LAPF detection model proposed in this paper introduces feature pyramid network and adds local attention mechanism. Combining bottom-up and top-down methods to obtain strong semantic features and enhance the learning of the underlying details, so as to improve the detection accuracy of transmission line insulator defect detection model. Secondly, this paper adds a local attention mechanism on the basis of FPN structure to extract feature information more accurately to alleviate the difficulty of small target detection, so as to improve the detection accuracy of small targets such as insulator defects of transmission lines. The experimental results of this paper show that the detection accuracy of LAPF detection model on the data set reaches 0.924, which fully demonstrates that the proposed improved model LAPF and target fusion data enhancement method are effective and necessary for realizing more accurate and general insulator defect detection in smart grid.

Author Keywords: Aerial image of transmission line insulators

articleTitle: Development of a Low Cost and Highly Efficient Hybrid Energy System for Rural Electrification
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: High cost of maintenance of electrical grid-extension and noise pollution and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission of Diesel Generator (DG) which are considered as the favorite energy sources for rural electrification necessitate the combination of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) as a viable solution. This paper determines the suitable blend of RES for electrification of Lemafu village in a bid to assess a low-cost investment of RES in Nigeria. The hybrid energy is achieved by mathematically modeling each component of the hybrid energy based on estimated load profile of the village. Then, BAT algorithm was employed as optimization technique to carried out optimal sizing and check the cost efficiency of the hybrid RES. Simulation was done using MATLAB R(2021a). The results showed that the hybrid RES with BAT algorithm for the village provide an appreciable reduction on the Cost of Energy (COE) production and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission with low cost of maintenance. This study would help power system operators in providing a good alternative to energy accessibility.

articleTitle: Interval Prediction Method for Wind Power Based on Informer-KAN
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: When employing the Informer model for wind power prediction, inherent noise in wind power datasets and the model's final layer's reliance on simplistic linear output have been observed to compromise the model's capacity for capturing nonlinear relationships, consequently resulting in suboptimal prediction accuracy. To address these limitations, a novel Informer-KAN wind power prediction model is proposed. The fully connected layers of the original Informer model are systematically replaced with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) layers constructed using cubic B-spline functions, which are designed to significantly enhance the model's capability for capturing complex nonlinear interactions and subsequently improve wind power prediction precision. Moreover, kernel density estimation is applied to the Informer-KAN model's predictions to generate probabilistic forecasts, enabling the derivation of power prediction intervals at varying confidence levels.

articleTitle: An Optimization Strategy for Electric Vehicle Aggregators to Participate in the Energy and Ancillary Services Market
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: This paper proposes an optimization strategy for Electric Vehicle (EV) aggregators to participate in the energy and ancillary services market. By analyzing the scheduling potential of EV clusters and their ability to generate revenue through charge-discharge strategies, an optimization model is developed to minimize total costs while considering constraints such as scheduling capacity, charge-discharge power, and battery state of charge (SOC). The results demonstrate that EVs, as distributed energy storage units, can support grid stability by providing frequency regulation services and achieve economic benefits by charging during low-price periods and discharging during high-price periods. Regional differences, such as residential, workplace, and commercial areas, influence EV participation in grid services. This strategy effectively balances grid loads, maximizes economic benefits, and improves energy storage efficiency, showcasing EV aggregators' significant role in the modern power system.

articleTitle: Trade-Off Planning of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations Based on Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: The surge in electric vehicles poses new challenges to charging stations, and a reasonable layout plan will promote the development of the electric vehicle industry. In the context of charging demand affected by seasonality, daily variations, we propose a method for the layout of electric vehicle charging stations calculated in granularity of hours. Firstly, based on the demand points after Monte Carlo simulation, we propose a dynamic time-varying charging station planning model with the optimization objectives of maximizing the annual revenue and minimizing user losses, under considering distance constraints, power constraints, queuing time constraints. To address this issue, we propose a two-stage search algorithm that combines random search with Whale Optimization Algorithm (RS-WOA) to find optimized solutions at both coarse and fine granularity levels. Finally, numerical simulation experiments were conducted in an example of the Optics Valley region in Wuhan, China. The experimental results show that our proposed algorithm achieved an annualized profit of 17.8399 million, which improved 5.3% and 37.7% compared to the RS algorithm and WOA algorithm, respectively.

articleTitle: Refined Analysis Method for Power Quantity Balance with High Proportion of New Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: With the continuous increase in the installed capacity of new energy such as wind power and photovoltaics, a high proportion of new energy power systems has become a trend for future development. However, wind power, photovoltaics, and hydropower vary greatly with the seasons, and the power system needs to meet the requirements of providing sufficient power supply during peak and off peak periods, as well as indicators such as wind and light curtailment when electricity consumption is low. In order to evaluate whether the newly added new energy electricity in the next year can be consumed, this paper proposes a refined analysis method for power grid electricity balance based on high proportion new energy. Through data-driven and genetic algorithm modeling of thermal power, hydropower, photovoltaic power, etc., the surplus electricity that meets the system load peak and valley is calculated, and based on this, whether the newly installed new energy capacity can be consumed is evaluated. According to the new energy installation plan of a certain province in China from 2024 to 2030, evaluate the on-site consumption capacity of new energy electricity in 2025 and 2030.

articleTitle: Research on Compressed Air Energy Storage Operation Optimization Based on New Energy Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: Driven by the global energy transition and dual-carbon targets, increasing the share of renewable energy in the energy mix has become a priority in the energy sector. Given the intermittent and unstable nature of renewable energy, compressed air energy storage (CAES) technology, with its large-scale energy storage potential and environmental adaptability, has become the key to balancing the supply and demand of power grids. In response to the neglect of the dynamic changes of CAES efficiency in existing studies, this paper proposes a new operation model to accurately simulate the dynamic efficiency of CAES under non-rated operating conditions. Then this paper explores the characteristics of compressor, turbine and storage chamber under wide operating conditions and constructs the corresponding steady-state thermodynamic simulation model. Further, this paper constructs a scheduling model of the combined wind-storage system to investigate the operating characteristics and their effects on the system operating efficiency. The results show that considering the wide operating characteristics of AA-CAES is essential to optimize the economy and operational flexibility of the wind storage system.

articleTitle: Research on Heating Terminal and Operation Regulation Strategy of Air Source Heat Pump in Rural Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: Air source heat pumps have gained widespread adoption as an efficient and environmentally friendly heating solution in rural areas of northern China. However, challenges such as poor insulation in rural buildings, significant fluctuations in user demand, and a lack of coordination in heating systems make it difficult for traditional heating regulation strategies to ensure efficient operation. Based on field testing, this study compares and analyzes the comfort levels provided by two heating terminal types: radiators and fan coils. By considering variations in outdoor air temperature, the research explores the application of combined quantity regulation and quality regulation to achieve dynamic control of the heating system. The findings indicate that fan coils are better suited for rural areas due to their simple and user-friendly volume adjustment, which enhances heating comfort and economic efficiency.

articleTitle: Harmonic Current Control and Application Based on APF in a Certain Research Institute
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: With the development of science and technology, the requirements of scientific research laboratories for power quality are becoming more and more strict. In order to solve the problem of power harmonics in scientific research laboratories, this paper analyzes the harm of power grid harmonics and the commonly used treatment methods. Several monitoring points that may produce harmonics in the experimental building were investigated, and the main harmonic sources in the building were identified. Through the analysis of the measured data, the corresponding control methods are selected. The results show that the combination of active filter and reactive power compensation cabinet can obviously filter out the harmonic current in the power grid system. The filtering rate is more than 85%, and the energy saving benefit is considerable.

articleTitle: Improved Control Strategy for Stationary Synchronous Compensator with Transient Voltage Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of voltage fluctuation of wind farm at the delivery end caused by reactive power surplus during DC fault, this paper proposes an improved control strategy of static synchronous regulator to suppress transient voltage. Firstly, we analyze the impact of DC system fault on the feeder voltage, and then we analyze the reactive power compensation characteristics of the synchronous regulator in different time scales with respect to the fault voltage characteristics; based on this, we put forward an improved control strategy for the regulator, which can be adapted to the different voltage compensation needs, and we also put forward a coordinated control strategy with the other reactive power voltage equipment of the wind farm, which can jointly inhibit the transient voltage after the fault. Based on the CIGRE standard model, the simulation model is carried out to verify the correctness and effectiveness of the method in this paper.

articleTitle: State of Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries Based on Support Vector Regression with Bayesian Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: Accurate prediction of the state of health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is essential for ensuring their safe and efficient operation. In this study, we developed a Bayesian hyperparameter-optimized support vector regression (SVR) with a Radial Basis Function (RBF) model to analyze the experimental battery data and estimated SOH. The charging voltage difference of an equal time interval was selected as a feature to indicate the status trend of the battery. Pearson correlation coefficients were applied to confirm the relationship between the feature indicator and the practical SOH. The Lowess smoothing technique enhances the precision of the feature extraction and machine learning models by reducing noise and capturing the underlying trends in noisy datasets. The model's effectiveness was verified through various experiments, including small voltage differences. The proposed method was applied to the NASA datasets, yielding accurate SOH estimations based on the evaluation matrices of the model.

articleTitle: A Method for Locating Fault Section of DC Lines Based on Signal Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: With the rapid development of modern power system, DC line plays an increasingly critical role. However, some traditional detection methods are difficult to identify and locate DC line faults effectively, and DC line fault location faces serious challenges. For improvement, this paper presents a new method of DC line fault section location based on the signal analysis by using intelligent electronic device (lED). The method collects the voltage data at the time of fault in real time, adopts the linear prediction coding algorithm, Hilbert transform, and combines the main frequency identification and instantaneous amplitude analysis to realize the accurate judgment of the fault section. Finally, simulation tests verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Compared with traditional methods, the proposed method has improved the accuracy of fault location and the clarity of indicators, which is helpful to solve the key problems in DC line fault detection.

articleTitle: Research on the Operation Strategy of Compressed Energy Storage in the Power Market Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: In the context of global energy structure transition and environmental protection, compressed air energy storage (CAES) technology has become the key to the enhancement of power system regulation due to its large-scale energy storage capacity, efficient energy conversion efficiency and environmental friendliness. The study uses a mixed integer linear programming model to investigate the economics of compressed air energy storage (CAES) power plants through price arbitrage and FM service market participation strategies in the peak-to-valley tariff system. It is found that CAES power plants charge during low tariff hours and discharge during high tariff hours to maximize profits and provide services in the FM market to increase revenues. The power plant's operating strategy is constrained by factors such as power caps, capacity limits, and self-discharge rates, which need to be allocated appropriately among different markets to optimize overall revenue. The results show that CAES power stations can effectively enhance their economic returns by participating in both price arbitrage and FM service markets under the peak-to-valley tariff system.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimal Scheduling Technology for Honeycomb Active Distribution Networks Based on Information Entropy
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: In the context of changes to the single-source radial network structure of active distribution networks, there exists the problem of inaccurate prediction of multi-user target loads, leading to significant power scheduling errors and high energy losses. To mitigate losses in distribution network systems and enhance the scheduling capabilities of distributed generation, a multi-objective optimal scheduling technology for honeycomb active distribution networks based on information entropy is proposed. By constructing a multi-objective optimal scheduling model for honeycomb active distribution networks, information entropy is utilized to quantify the uncertainty of different scheduling schemes. A multi-objective load scheduling model for distribution networks is designed, and a self-adaptive particle swarm optimization algorithm based on distribution entropy is adopted to propose the solution method and process for the model. Experimental results show that after applying this technology, the distribution network system loss is reduced, the operational stability of the distribution network is improved, and flexible scheduling and efficient utilization of distributed generation are achieved.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Status Quo and Development Trend of New Energy Storage Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: New energy storage technologies, as the key to building a new energy system, are experiencing rapid growth and technological diversification. The government work report first proposed the development of new energy storage, marking its important position in national economic development. This article analyzes the advantages, challenges, and development trends of main new energy storage technologies, including lithium-ion batteries, sodium-ion batteries, flow batteries, compressed air energy storage, flywheel energy storage, gravity energy storage, thermal energy storage, supercapacitor energy storage, and hydrogen energy storage. Overall, new energy storage technologies are gradually moving from the initial commercialization stage to the scaled development stage, with significant improvements in innovation capabilities and a substantial increase in the level of independent control over core technology equipment. In the future, new energy storage technologies need to address their respective challenges to support the safe and stable operation of high-proportion new energy power systems and promote high-quality social progress.

articleTitle: Assessment Method for Potential Carbon Reduction in Electricity Considering Marginal Cost-Effectiveness
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: In response to the fact that the construction of China's carbon and electricity markets is still in its early stages, and due to the positive superposition of electricity carbon marginal costs and the bidirectional impact of carbon emissions and power generation plans, power companies are under enormous cost pressure to achieve carbon reduction targets, therefore, a carbon reduction potential assessment method considering marginal cost-effectiveness is proposed. This method first calculates the carbon reduction potential of a single carbon reduction measure for power grid enterprises, analyzes the carbon reduction amount and cost of a single carbon reduction measure. Then, with the goal of maximizing carbon assets and minimizing emission reduction costs, the marginal cost-effectiveness is considered to calculate the carbon reduction potential of power grid enterprises, under the constraints of various carbon reduction measures and the balance of electricity supply and demand, effectively transferring the bid winning electricity in the electricity market from high pollution dyeing motors to cleaner generators can promote the reduction of carbon emissions in the power system and achieve the goal of carbon emission constraints for power grid enterprises, at the same time, during high load periods, the cost of carbon reduction is transmitted to consumers by increasing carbon conductivity, ensuring the overall income level of the power industry.

Author Keywords: assessment of carbon emission reduction potential

articleTitle: Cost-Benefit Accounting for Pumped Storage Power Plants Under the Two-Pronged Tariff System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: Pumped storage is the most mature technology, the best economy, the most large-scale development conditions of the power system green low-carbon clean and flexible regulation power. With the improvement of pumped storage power plant management system, the number of projects has increased dramatically, but the pumped storage power plant is still not connected with the market development. This paper constructs a cost accounting model and a benefit accounting model for pumped storage power plants under the two-part tariff system, and analyzes the economic benefits and return on capital under different operation modes based on the examples of pumped storage power plants, which is of great significance to support the reasonable recovery of the capacity cost of pumped storage power plants as well as to effectively avoid the investment risk of pumped storage power plants.

articleTitle: A comparative Study of Multiple Deep Neural Network Architectures and XGBoost Model in Electricity Price Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: In addressing the complexity of electricity market price fluctuations, this study reviews various electricity price forecasting methods and their application effectiveness. By employing time series analysis and principles of machine learning, a comparison is made between traditional methods such as ARIMA and VAR, and machine learning algorithms including XGBoost and LSTM. This approach theoretically enhances the ability of electricity price forecasting to capture nonlinear data and multidimensional complex interactions. Experiments focused on electricity price prediction demonstrate that machine learning methods outperform traditional techniques in terms of accuracy. Specifically, XGBoost achieves efficient data fitting, LSTM excels at handling long time series data, and the CNN-LSTM combined model is particularly adept at capturing both local and global features of price changes, leading to further improvements in predictive accuracy. These findings indicate that the proposed methods exhibit significant advancements in forecasting precision.

articleTitle: Optimization Strategy for Joint Day Dispatch of Pumped Storage Thermal Power Plants Based on Dynamic Frequency Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: With the increase of the proportion of new energy connected to the grid and replacing some synchronous units, the virtual inertia of new energy has not been widely used, which leads to the problems of the decline of the system inertia level and the decline of frequency stability. Due to its natural advantages, pumped storage units can provide inertia support like traditional synchronous units when they are in the state of power generation, and enhance the frequency stability of power grid; When the pump is in the pumping state, it can also cut off the pump quickly to offset the unbalanced power caused by the disturbance. Therefore, this paper takes pumped storage as the starting point, discusses the frequency modulation strategy, and establishes the frequency constraint to ensure the frequency stability based on the inertia index. The effectiveness of the frequency modulation strategy and model proposed in this paper is proved by a numerical example. The addition of pumped storage can greatly improve the anti disturbance ability of the system and enhance the frequency stability of the system.

articleTitle: Optimized Scheduling of Flexibility Resources for Source-Grid-Load-Storage Based on Improved Wind-Solar Scenario Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: In response to the issues of voltage fluctuations and increased system losses caused by the volatility of wind and solar generation in the optimal scheduling of source-grid-load-storage, an optimized scheduling method for flexibility resources based on improved wind-solar scenario clustering is proposed. Firstly, an improved wind-solar scenario clustering algorithm is introduced, which combines density noise-based spatial clustering (DBSCAN) and iterative self-organizing data analysis (ISODATA) techniques to achieve accurate clustering and optimization of wind-solar scenarios. The clustering performance is evaluated using the DB index, Dunn index, and silhouette coefficient to ensure the scientific and stable results. Secondly, considering the crucial role of flexibility resources in source-grid-load-storage scheduling, an optimization model based on flexibility resources is proposed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through simulations on the IEEE 33-bus system. The results show that the optimized scheduling method can significantly improve the scheduling efficiency of flexibility resources, reduce operational costs, and ensure the stability and sustainability of coordinated source-grid-load-storage operation in a low-carbon economy context.

articleTitle: Research on a New Voltage Balance Modulation Technique for Series Connection of SiC MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: When multiple SiC MOSFETs are operated in series, they are affected by inconsistencies in parasitic parameters or peripheral circuit parameters, resulting in unbalanced device drain-source voltages in the series branch. Aiming at this problem, the article firstly proposes a new voltage balancing modulation technique combining power-side voltage balancing and driver-side voltage balancing. The circuit consists of four parts, including a snubber circuit, a clamp circuit, a coupled inductor voltage balancing circuit, and a closed-loop control circuit for the drive signal, and has the advantages of modularity, low extra loss, and fast voltage balancing. Secondly, the article also describes the method of parameter design for each part of the circuit. Finally, the feasibility of this voltage-balanced modulation technique and the practicality of the parameter design are verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Analysis of Energy Consumption of Road Cold Chain Transportation Under Different Refrigeration Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: With the rapid growth of cold chain logistics demand, promoting the green and low-carbon transformation of road cold chain transport has received more and more attention. The calculation of transport energy consumption is still the key problem. Researchers have studied the calculation methods of cold chain transport energy consumption in different refrigeration modes. However, there is a lack of further analysis on the combination of vehicle energy supply mode and refrigeration mode. In this paper, we propose four combined modes of refrigeration and power energy technologies. In the given urban distribution scenario, the energy consumption of different modes is estimated and compared. Results show that for fuel refrigerated trucks, the passive storage mode can effectively reduce the transport energy consumption and reduce the energy consumption cost compared with mechanical refrigeration mode. While for electric refrigerated trucks, the difference in energy consumption is not obvious. It is necessary select the mode according to the specific application scenario. This study has important reference significance for putting forward technical solutions that can meet the needs of constant temperature freshness preservation and satisfy the requirements of green and low-carbon development in the industry.

articleTitle: Optimized Scheduling of Multi-Energy Coupled Virtual Power Plants for Low-Carbon Economic Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: With the global emphasis on reducing greenhouse gas emissions, traditional power generation methods are facing challenges, highlighting the importance of dispatching distributed energy. This paper addresses the issues of resource allocation and low-carbon operational model transformation in Multi-Energy Coupled Virtual Power Plants (MECVPPs) by establishing a low-carbon economic dispatch model for MECVPPs. Furthermore, an improved Common Coot Optimization Technique (COOT) is designed to solve this model. Simulation experiments validate the effectiveness and practicability of the model in terms of resource dispatching and demand-side response, providing guidance for the low-carbon economic operation and dispatch of MECVPPs.

articleTitle: A Photovoltaic Load Predictive Control Model of Microgrid Based on Secondary Frequency Conversion under Random Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: With the increasing application rate of renewable energy and distributed generators based on power electronics technology in microgrid, its high random and low inertia power disturbance bring more problems to frequency control. In order to solve these problems, this article put forward a micro grid photovoltaic predictive control model with secondary frequency regulation under random conditions. The control strategy includes unknown input observers. RESs/DGs uses load virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control to increase the inertia of the system. In order to improve the effect of predictive control, unknown input observers are used to estimate the system state and random power disturbances. By overcoming the quadratic programming (QP) optimization problem with variable constraints, the distributed recovery power of each DG is received. By setting appropriate weighting factors, RESs/DGs can participate in secondary frequency control preferentially. An island microgrid model composed of photovoltaic power sources is established. Compared with the general secondary control system, this system improves the system frequency, increases the recovery speed, and diminishs the frequency deviation.

articleTitle: Optimization and Development Methods for Data Asset Management in Power Systems Based on Knowledge Graphs
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: With the increasing complexity and intelligence of modern power systems, the volume of data has grown exponentially, covering various stages from generation, transmission, and distribution to consumption. Traditional data management methods struggle to handle the vast data volume and complex data relationships, resulting in data silos and information asymmetry, which limit the efficiency and decision-making capabilities of power systems. Knowledge graphs, as an emerging data management technology, integrate data and knowledge to provide a global view of data relationships and intelligent analysis capabilities. This paper proposes an optimization method for data asset management in power systems based on knowledge graphs, discussing the construction of knowledge graphs, data processing techniques, and their application in power systems to enhance data management and intelligence levels.

articleTitle: Research on Trusted Capacity of New Energy with Storage under Spot Market Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: The randomness, intermittency, and volatility of new energy pose new challenges to the planning and operation of traditional power systems. Therefore, it is necessary to accurately evaluate the role and value of new energy and energy storage equipment in the power system. Firstly, based on the rules of Shandong Electric Power spot market, analyzes its market structure, trading process, price mechanism, operation mode, and settlement mechanism. Secondly, a new energy credible capacity calculation method based on a certain confidence level and historical data was determined for typical scenarios of wind farm storage and photovoltaic power station storage on the source side of the power system. Then, based on the current market electricity price under the conditions of the electricity spot market, with the goal of maximizing profits, the timing of energy storage output is determined, and the reliable capacity of new energy with storage is further determined. Optimization is carried out on a daily basis to determine the reliable capacity of new energy distribution and storage under different time periods, and to determine the value of improved reliable capacity. Finally, based on the historical output of new energy in a certain province and recent market electricity price data, the impact of energy storage charging and discharging behavior on the reliable capacity of new energy with storage in the power grid at different time periods is determined. Under the conditions of the spot market, based on the behavior of market entities, the proposed method for calculating the reliable capacity of new energy with storage can meet the supply guarantee needs of the power grid, and the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method are verified. This study contributes to promoting the application of new energy with storage in ensuring power grid reliability and provides a basis for the calculation of reliable capacity for new energy with storage.

articleTitle: Resilient and Profitable Peer-to-peer Energy Transactions in Microgrids Using Coalitional Game Theory and Incentive Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: The growth of decentralized renewable energy generation has led to the development of peer-to-peer (P2P) energy transactions, enabling direct energy exchange between users within community microgrids. This paper presents a resilient P2P energy trading framework using coalitional game theory to address renewable energy generation and load demand uncertainties. The framework allows prosumers to form coalitions, optimizing energy transactions by managing resources collectively. Contract constraints are designed to control risks to incentivize participation and ensure secure and predictable outcomes. A Shapley value-based payoff scheme ensures fair profit distribution, fostering cooperation within the coalition. Comprehensive simulations validate the framework's effectiveness in managing uncertainties, optimizing profits, and enhancing microgrid resilience. The results demonstrate the potential of coalitional game theory in enabling sustainable and profitable P2P energy trading, offering a robust solution for improving the reliability and economic viability of decentralized energy systems amid increasing renewable energy adoption.

articleTitle: A Vehicle-by- Vehicle Charging Scheduling Strategy for Residential Areas Considering Grid-level Valley Filling
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: In recent years, as the penetration of electric vehicles (EVs) gradually increases, the problem that some residential areas are unable to accept more EVs due to the tight power supply capacity is becoming more and more prominent. The capacity of existing power supply facilities in a neighborhood to accept EV s can be improved by orderly charging control. To provide a feasible orderly charging control method for residential communities facing difficulties in upgrading distribution facilities, this paper proposes a vehicle-by-vehicle charging scheduling strategy, which can adapt to different residential communities with varying power supply capacities by adjusting the valley-filling time periods. For neighborhoods with non-stressed and generally stressed power supply capacity, setting the valley filling sequence to the grid valley and subsequent flat periods enables peak shaving and valley filling at the grid level while the user receives the lowest charging tariff. Example analysis shows that when the user participation degree is 80%, compared with disordered charging, this strategy reduces the average charging prices of users by 0.3627 yuan, and reduces the peak-valley difference of the total load at the grid level by 17.19%. For severely constrained power supply capacity neighborhoods, the time period for valley filling is set to 0-24:00 p.m. Example analyses show that under the current neighborhood conditions, EV acceptance of the number of households can be achieved at 80% user participation and there is room for continued acceptance.

articleTitle: Fault Control Method of New Energy Through Flexible DC System Based on Coordination of Stability Control and Energy Dissipation Device
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: Due to the difficulty in matching the development speed of voltage and current after the failure of the DC power grid and the time to cut off the new energy unit through the AC safety control device, any disturbance may cause the surplus power of the DC power grid, which will lead to a large-scale paralysis of the DC power grid. To solve this problem, this paper takes a DC network as an example to analyze the surplus power of DC network and analyzes the adaptability of energy-consuming devices to consume surplus power. On this basis, a new DC energy-consuming topology is designed, and its parameters are designed, and the switching strategy of energy-consuming devices is put forward. Finally, the coordinated control strategy between the energy-consuming device and the stable control system is proposed. The simulation results show that this method can effectively improve the fault ride-through ability of the new energy to send out the system fault through flexibility.

articleTitle: Analysis of Issues and Countermeasures for the Synergistic Linkage Between Electricity and Carbon Markets
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: In the context of global warming, China has proposed the “dual carbon” (carbon peaking and carbon neutrality) targets, with the power industry playing a pivotal role as a major contributor to carbon emissions, and its decarbonization transformation being of utmost importance. This paper firstly elucidates the significance of the linkage between the electricity market and the carbon market, introduces the operational mechanism of the carbon market and the linkage mechanism between the electricity and carbon markets, and reviews the current status and development history of China's carbon market. Through an examination of data on carbon emission allowance trading in the national carbon market, this paper delves into the issues surrounding the coordinated linkage between the electricity and carbon markets, including imperfections in the price transmission mechanism and deficiencies in the mutual recognition system. To address these issues, the paper proposes countermeasures such as optimizing the carbon market pricing mechanism, improving coordination mechanisms, enhancing dynamic quota adjustments, providing policy support for renewable energy participation, establishing pilot projects for linkage, increasing the proportion of carbon market quota auctions, promoting policy coordination, refining the mutual recognition system, and establishing a bidirectional incentive mechanism. These measures aim to facilitate the coordinated development of the electricity and carbon markets and achieve the “dual carbon” targets.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Classification of Typical Joint Scenarios in Power Systems Based on Improved Iterative Selforganizing Data Analysis Technique Algorithm and Feature Hierarchical Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: With the increasing proportion of renewable energy in the power system, the load, photovoltaic and wind power characteristics show complex dynamic changes, and the traditional single-element scenario classification method is difficult to cope with this challenge. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes a two-stage typical joint scene classification method for power systems based on improved iterative selforganizing data analysis technique algorithm (ISODATA) and elemental hierarchical clustering. In the first stage, for load, photovoltaic (PV) and wind power time-series data, the improved ISODATA algorithm is used to reconstruct the time-series data by variance and extreme variance thresholds to consider local differences, and combined with the composite Euclidean dynamic time warping (DTW) metrics to measure the overall differences, which optimizes the classification accuracy of the single-element time-series. In the second stage, on the basis of the elemental typical scenes obtained in the first stage, the interrelationships and dynamic change characteristics of load, PV and wind power are analyzed, the relevant feature quantities are set, and the elements are jointly analyzed by using the hierarchical clustering method, and a typical joint scene of multiple elements is finally obtained. The joint scene not only integrates the characteristics of multiple elements, but also is more complex and comprehensive than the single-element scene. The experimental results show that the method proposed in this paper can effectively improve the accuracy of typical scene classification, accurately capture the complex change characteristics of various elements in the power system, and provide strong data support for intelligent scheduling and optimization.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-scenario Inter-provincial Power Transmission Strategy Based on Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: With the advancement of electricity market reform, inter-provincial electricity trading faces many challenges. Traditional strategies for inter-provincial transmission are difficult to adapt to the complex environment, while reinforcement learning has the capabilities of autonomous learning, decision optimization, and environmental adaptability. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-scenario method for inter-provincial transmission based on reinforcement learning. Firstly, different confidence level scenario sets are generated based on the multi-temporal source-load power prediction of LSTM (Long Short Memory) and the established evaluation index system. Secondly, an inter-provincial transmission strategy model based on the PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) algorithm is established based on the benefit model for inter-provincial transmission, and the optimal strategy is obtained through training and optimization. Finally, through case analysis, the source-load power prediction results, the PPO algorithm training results, and the inter-provincial transmission results under different scenarios are presented, with the expectation of providing support for decision-making in the inter-provincial electricity market.

articleTitle: A Multi-Stage Collaborative Optimization Operation Method for Distribution-Microgrid for Reliability Improvement
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: In recent years, micro grids have played an increasingly important role in the construction of new type power systems This also renders distribution networks (DN), characterized by comparatively weaker structural resilience, increasingly susceptible to extensive and prolonged outages in the event of faults. This paper proposes a multi-stage coordinated optimization method for distribution-microgrid systems based on flexible soft-switching. In the pre-disaster phase, a preventive model is developed to deploy mobile energy storage and adjust operating modes. During the disaster phase, measures such as switch isolation and mobile energy storage power regulation are implemented. In the post-disaster phase, a scheduling model for mobile energy storage and construction teams is integrated to form a multi-stage coordinated optimization model. The model is then formulated as a bilevel mixed-integer linear programming problem and solved iteratively using the Column and Constraint Generation (C&CG) algorithm to achieve optimal resource allocation. Case studies demonstrate that the SOP-based multi-stage distribution-microgrid cooperative optimization strategy significantly improves power supply continuity for loads during faults, reduces restoration times, and enhances overall grid reliability.

articleTitle: Real-Time Simulation Testbed for Energy Management and Control of Renewable Energy-Based Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: This paper presents a real-time simulation testbed designed to evaluate energy management and control strategies for renewable energy-based microgrids. The testbed is developed using a real-time digital simulator (RTDS) to assess the performance of control methods before practical implementation. The microgrid model incorporates key renewable and storage components, encompassing photovoltaic (PV) generation, battery storage, a diesel generator, and a vehicle-to-grid-enabled electric vehicle (EV) charging station. The research emphasizes three operational scenarios: grid-connected operation, smooth transition to islanded mode with the battery inverter operating in grid-forming mode, and islanded operation employing the emergency generator when the battery is completely discharged. By simulating these conditions, the testbed allows for a comprehensive analysis of system stability, energy efficiency, and reliability under real-world conditions, thereby ensuring that the developed control strategies can effectively manage power flow and system stability in both connected and islanded modes. The results provide valuable insights into optimizing microgrid operations.

articleTitle: Purchase Strategy of Electricity Retailer Considering Electric Vehicles with Renewable Portfolio System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: Under the renewable portfolio standards (RPS), electricity retailers are obliged to absorb renewable energy. In addition to the purchase of conventional electricity, electricity retailer also needs to purchase corresponding power products in the green electricity contract market and green certificate market to fulfill the consumption responsibility. In order to enhance the inertia of the power system, electric vehicle (EV) can be used as a flexible and low-cost energy storage device through vehicle-grid (V2G) interaction technology. In the face of several power products with different price fluctuations, electricity retailers should comprehensively evaluate the cost and risk of power purchase, and optimize the power purchase ratio to maximize the overall benefit. In this paper, the conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) is used to quantify the risk, and the dual-objective optimization model with the lowest risk and the lowest purchase cost is constructed, which is transformed into a single objective problem of the minimum expected electricity purchase cost under the constraint of CVaR, and is solved by using the CPLEX solver. Through the case study, the application effect of the model in different market development periods and different quota targets is verified, which is of great significance for electricity retailer to optimize the electricity purchase strategy and achieve long-term development, and provides a reference for the improvement of the electricity market mechanism, the promotion of V2G interaction, and the optimization of renewable energy policies.

articleTitle: Vector Retrieval-Based Intelligent Q&A System for Offshore Power Transmission and Substation Projects
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Symposium on New Energy and Electrical Technology (ISNEET)
abstract: Current systems for designing transmission and substations struggle with complex marine environmental impacts and enhancing efficiency for cross-sea lines, requiring intelligent, automated solutions. This paper presents an intelligent Q&A system for cross-sea transmission engineering, focusing on anti-corrosion material selection, construction methods, and maintenance strategies. The system combines vector retrieval and natural language generation to provide rapid and accurate access to design information and generate personalized solutions. It constructs a knowledge vector database and employs Grouped Query Attention (GQA) and Dual-Block Attention (DCA) mechanisms for optimized knowledge retrieval. Additionally, it uses prompt engineering and multi-round dialogue mechanisms to enhance design schemes and system intelligence. Experimental results show that the system significantly improves design efficiency and response speed, meeting the industry's need for efficient and intelligent design support.
